clue.text: The great resourcefulness for which Croesus was noted

definitions.text: The great resourcefulness for which Croesus was noted

parts.words: The great resourcefulness for which Croesus was noted
parts.note: resourcefulness is read as being full of resources, money above all: the legendary riches of the Lydian king

explanation.surface: A tribute to the ingenuity of an ancient king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resourcefulness' suggests cleverness, but here it means having vast resources; Croesus, king of Lydia, was proverbial for his riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus is the byword for limitless riches, which is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Succeeds in understanding the argument?

definitions.meaning: comes after, takes the place of
grasps the reasoning, as in 'I follow you'

explanation.definitionFit: One thing comes after another in sequence; to grasp a line of reasoning is to keep up with it.

clue.text: Statistical overstatement of a sporting nature

definitions.text: Statistical overstatement of a sporting nature

parts.words: Statistical overstatement of a sporting nature
parts.note: overstatement is split as over statement: in cricket the record of overs bowled, runs given and wickets taken

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled; a bowler's figures list overs, maidens, runs and wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler's figures are the statistics of his overs.

clue.text: The German song Old Nick turned up in Scotland

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Old Nick is the devil, which in Scotland is the Deil

explanation.surface: Satan appears north of the border singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Scotland' asks for the Scots word for the devil, DEIL, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is an art song in German, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Type of overcoat to which a part of the British Army is committed

definitions.meaning: a long loose overcoat with a cape

definitions.text: to which a part of the British Army is committed
definitions.meaning: Northern Ireland, where British troops were deployed

explanation.definitionFit: The province of Northern Ireland gave its name to a heavy belted coat; troops were posted there in the Troubles.

clue.text: An extra bed shaken up with a will?

indicators.note: shaken up says these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Disturbing a bed while making a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken up' rearranges BED and A WILL. In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery out of the batter's reach concedes a run that counts as an extra in cricket.

clue.text: A semblance of a court ta presentation, maybe

definitions.meaning: turning up before a judge, or being presented at Court

explanation.walkthrough: The 'ta' in the clue as held is print debris; the second sense is a court presentation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means outward look, and also turning up to answer in front of a judge.

clue.text: Consider matters finished? in 10

parts.note: judge that affairs are at an end

explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something carefully before deciding.

clue.text: Position of rider on a steed, at could be

indicators.note: could be says the letters might be arranged as something else

explanation.surface: Where a horseman sits on his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges A STEED; 'at' is a stray in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider in the saddle is sitting down on the horse.

clue.text: Wild wild Wales in the 50s

indicators.note: in places the shuffled country inside the pair of letters for the fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50, so the plural 50s is L's, LS

indicators.note: wild says the letters of the country's name run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A Western-style picture of untamed Welsh life in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Wild' is the definition and the second the anagram signal; '50s' is read as two Roman fifties, L's, rather than a decade.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless country is wild and untamed, without order.

clue.text: Indulge in some asset-stripping, apparently?

parts.note: taking away someone's assets is to strip them of what they have

explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of what they own is to take it from them, leaving them without.

clue.text: Classical poet I'd nothing against initially

indicators.note: initially says the nothing and the against come at the start, ahead of the I'd

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A poet who had nothing to object to at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' puts O (nothing) and V (versus, 'against') before ID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman author of the Metamorphoses is a poet of classical antiquity.

clue.text: Joy's enemy might fight fire with this

definitions.meaning: a killjoy who dampens everyone's fun
a soaked cover thrown over flames smothers them

explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy damps down fun as a soaked cover damps down flames.

clue.text: The drink of the masses? 01

parts.note: masses read as church Masses, not ordinary people

explanation.surface: Asking what the common people drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masses' suggests the populace, but it is the Mass, the Eucharist where consecrated wine is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine consecrated at the Eucharist is the drink of the Mass.

clue.text: Remarkable piece of railway equipment

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, notable or striking
the trackside device that tells trains to stop or go

explanation.definitionFit: A signal success is outstanding; a railway signal is the lineside stop-and-go light or arm.

clue.text: Unnaturally pale apprentice outwardly stranded?

indicators.note: outwardly means the stranded word sits on the outside of the apprentice letter

parts.note: a stranded whale or boat is beached
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee left high and dry, looking pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a British learner driver, hence L for a learner or apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or cloth whitened with chemicals has been made pale artificially.

clue.text: Army formation left on the fo Cumbrian coast

indicators.note: formation means the letters are formed into a new shape

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Troops drawn up and abandoned by the sea in north-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges ARMY; 'fo' is print debris. The town is a harbour in Cumbria, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The harbour town lies on the Solway shore of Cumbria.

clue.text: It has to be fed in different manner

indicators.note: different asks for the letters in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions for feeding a creature in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is kept as written; 'different' rearranges MANNER to NERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a humorous term for one's stomach or appetite, which must be fed.

clue.text: The territorial detachment founder Ulysses's command

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The territorial detachment founder Ulysses's command' looks garbled by OCR; no parse of the first part gives ITHACA and no search found the original
annotationWithheld.clue: The territorial detachment founder Ulysses's command

clue.text: A fine Oxonian candlestick

definitions.meaning: at Oxford colleges, a penalty of drinking ale imposed for breaches of table etiquette
a candle holder fixed to a wall

explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford the word is a forfeit at dinner; it is also a wall bracket holding candles.

clue.text: Palace official who might be asked tricky query about his to Royal mistress?

indicators.note: about means the jumbled question goes round the royal letters
tricky indicates the letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A courtier questioned about his relations with the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges QUERY to EQURY, which goes 'about' ER (the Queen).
explanation.definitionFit: A royal attendant officer in the household of the sovereign.

clue.text: Trollope booked a prison offcer officer

definitions.meaning: the title of the first Barchester novel by Anthony Trollope
the governor or guard of a jail

explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's 1855 novel bears this title, and it is also the term for a jail's chief official.

clue.text: Unemployment benefit for the rest of the year?

definitions.text: Unemployment benefit for the rest of the year?

parts.words: Unemployment benefit for the rest of the year?
parts.note: not working for a spell each year, yet still being paid: money during annual leave rather than a dole

explanation.surface: A complaint about the welfare system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unemployment benefit' looks like the dole, but it is money paid while you rest from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages paid during annual leave are money received while not working.

clue.text: Thesaurus's definition of one who sold birthright for a bowl of soup

definitions.text: one who sold birthright for a bowl of soup

indicators.note: the definition is found inside the word, so its letters lie within the reference book's name

explanation.surface: Looking up a biblical character in a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Jacob's brother sold his birthright for a mess of pottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis tells of Isaac's elder son trading his birthright to Jacob for a meal of stew.

clue.text: A high speed piece of film

definitions.meaning: a fast pace, as in going at a good lick
a short extract from a movie

explanation.definitionFit: A brisk pace is a good one, and a short excerpt shown from a movie is the other sense.

clue.text: Casinos designed for a place near Naples

indicators.note: designed signals the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Gambling halls built for an Italian resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges CASINOS; the town lies between Rome and Naples, under Monte Cassino.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian town is in Lazio, in the region south towards Naples.

clue.text: Free to give a door-to door service

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to set free, rescue

definitions.text: to give a door-to door service
definitions.meaning: to bring goods or post to each house

explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to free them; a postman's round brings mail to each home.

clue.text: A compliant personality?

parts.note: party is read as a person in a deal, one who agrees

explanation.definitionFit: A party is one side in an agreement; one who consents is a compliant participant.
